concepts.title: Distance Formula Between Two Points
concepts.definition: The straight-line separation between any two coordinate positions in a Cartesian plane obtained by applying the Pythagorean principle to horizontal and vertical spans.
concepts.key_idea: Square root of the sum of squared differences of corresponding coordinates.
question_patterns: find the distance between the points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)
calculate the length of the line segment joining two given points
what is the distance separating the pairs of coordinate points
determine the separation between two locations on a coordinate plane
how far apart are two points on the Cartesian grid

solution_steps.explain: find square of difference in x coordinates
find square of difference in y coordinates
take square root of the sum of squared horizontal and vertical differences

concepts.title: Distance of a Point from the Origin
concepts.definition: The length of the line segment connecting the origin to any specified point in the coordinate system.
concepts.key_idea: Radial distance is the square root of the sum of squares of the abscissa and ordinate.
question_patterns: find the distance of the point (x, y) from the origin
calculate how far a given point lies from (0, 0)
determine the distance between the origin and a given location
what is the separation between (0, 0) and the point (x, y)
compute the radial distance of a point from the origin

solution_steps.explain: add the square of the x-coordinate to the square of the y-coordinate
evaluate square root of the sum of squares

concepts.title: Collinearity of Three Points
concepts.definition: A geometric condition where three distinct points reside on a single continuous straight line, verified when the sum of two pairwise segment lengths equals the third.
concepts.key_idea: Three points lie on one line if the largest segment length equals the sum of the other two.
question_patterns: determine if the three given points are collinear
check whether the points lie on the same straight line
verify if the given set of three points is collinear using distance formula
show that three coordinates form a single continuous line
test if three given locations are situated along a straight path

solution_steps.explain: use distance formula to calculate lengths AB, BC, and AC between the three points

solution_steps.action: compare sum of shorter lengths to longest length
solution_steps.explain: check if the sum of the two smaller distances is equal to the largest distance
state that the points are collinear if equality holds, or non-collinear otherwise

concepts.title: Equidistant Points and Coordinate Loci
concepts.definition: A condition in which a point maintains identical spatial separation from two or more reference points, creating an algebraic constraint or perpendicular bisector relation.
concepts.key_idea: Equating squared distances eliminates radicals to find unknown coordinates or linear relations.

find the point on the x-axis which is equidistant from two points
find a relation between x and y such that (x, y) is equidistant from two points

solution_steps.explain: let P be the point and equate squared distances PA^2 = PB^2 to avoid radical terms
expand binomial squares and cancel quadratic terms from both sides

solution_steps.explain: isolate the unknown variable or simplify to obtain the required linear relation

concepts.title: Section Formula for Internal Division
concepts.definition: A coordinate formulation determining the position of a partition point that divides an interval joining two given points in a specified internal ratio.
concepts.key_idea: Weighted average of coordinates weighted inversely by ratio distances.
question_patterns: find the coordinates of the point dividing a line segment in a given ratio
calculate the point that divides the join of two points internally in ratio m1:m2
determine the division point on a line segment with a given internal ratio
what are the coordinates of the dividing point for ratio k:1
find the position of a point dividing the segment joining A and B

solution_steps.explain: assign x1, y1, x2, y2 and the ratio values m1, m2

solution_steps.action: compute x coordinate of division point
solution_steps.explain: evaluate x = (m1*x2 + m2*x1) / (m1 + m2)

solution_steps.action: compute y coordinate of division point
solution_steps.explain: evaluate y = (m1*y2 + m2*y1) / (m1 + m2)
write the final coordinates as an ordered pair (x, y)

concepts.title: Mid-point Formula
concepts.definition: A specific instance of section division where an interval is halved equally, resulting in coordinates that are arithmetic means of the endpoints.
concepts.key_idea: The midpoint coordinates are the arithmetic averages of the respective endpoint coordinates.
question_patterns: find the midpoint of the line segment joining two given points

concepts.title: Determining Ratio of Division
concepts.definition: The algebraic procedure to discover the proportional segment split made by a known point or coordinate axis upon a line segment.
concepts.key_idea: Representing ratio as k:1 allows solving a single linear equation in one unknown.

concepts.title: Trisection of a Line Segment
concepts.definition: Dividing a line segment into three equal lengths using two intermediate partition points that split the segment in ratios 1:2 and 2:1.
concepts.key_idea: Two trisection points divide the total segment internally in ratios 1:2 and 2:1.
question_patterns: find the coordinates of the points of trisection of a line segment

solution_steps.action: apply 1:2 ratio for first trisection point

solution_steps.action: apply 2:1 ratio or midpoint method for second point

concepts.title: Area of Rhombus via Diagonal Lengths
concepts.definition: The planar area enclosed by a rhombus computed as half the product of the lengths of its two perpendicular diagonals.
concepts.key_idea: Diagonal lengths found using distance formula multiplied and halved yield rhombus area.
question_patterns: find the area of a rhombus given its four vertices in order

determine the area of rhombus ABCD given coordinates of its vertices
what is the area enclosed by a rhombus whose vertices are known
compute the area of a rhombus using the lengths of its diagonals

solution_steps.explain: find product of the two diagonal lengths d1 and d2
divide product of diagonals by 2 to obtain area

questions: 1. Find the distance between the following pairs of points : (i) (2, 3), (4, 1) (ii) (-5, 7), (-1, 3) (iii) (a, b), (-a, -b)

3. Determine if the points (1, 5), (2, 3) and (-2, -11) are collinear.
4. Check whether (5, -2), (6, 4) and (7, -2) are the vertices of an isosceles triangle.
5. In a classroom, 4 friends are seated at points A, B, C and D as shown in Fig. 7.8. Champa asks Chameli if ABCD is a square. Using distance formula, find which of them is correct.
6. Name the type of quadrilateral formed, if any, by the following points: (i) (-1, -2), (1, 0), (-1, 2), (-3, 0) (ii) (-3, 5), (3, 1), (0, 3), (-1, -4) (iii) (4, 5), (7, 6), (4, 3), (1, 2)
7. Find the point on the x-axis which is equidistant from (2, -5) and (-2, 9).
8. Find the values of y for which the distance between the points P(2, -3) and Q(10, y) is 10 units.
9. If Q(0, 1) is equidistant from P(5, -3) and R(x, 6), find the values of x. Also find the distances QR and PR.
10. Find a relation between x and y such that the point (x, y) is equidistant from the point (3, 6) and (-3, 4).
1. Find the coordinates of the point which divides the join of (-1, 7) and (4, -3) in the ratio 2 : 3.
2. Find the coordinates of the points of trisection of the line segment joining (4, -1) and (-2, -3).

4. Find the ratio in which the line segment joining (-3, 10) and (6, -8) is divided by (-1, 6).
